I: B1 [ I ] to experience physical or mental pain

I or T: B2 [ I or T ] to experience or show the effects of something bad

example: I think he suffered a lot when his wife left him.
我想他妻子離開他時，他一定很痛苦。
She suffers in the winter when it's cold and her joints get stiff.
冬天天氣寒冷，她的關節會變得僵硬，這讓她非常難受。
She's been suffering from (= been ill with) cancer for two years.
她患癌症已經兩年了。
Johnny suffers from (= is often ill with) asthma.
約翰尼患有哮喘。
Do you suffer from (= do you have) any allergies?
你對任何物質過敏嗎？
If you're not happy with it, you should complain. Don't just suffer in silence (= without saying anything).
如果你不喜歡，應該說出來。別悶在心裡。
The Democrats suffered a crushing defeat in the last election.
民主黨在上次選舉中慘敗。
25 policemen suffered minor injuries during the riots.
抗議事件中有25名員警受到輕傷。
The city suffered another blow last month with the closure of the local car factory.
當地汽車廠上個月倒閉，這是該市受到的又一打擊。
If you go and eat three helpings of dessert, you'll just have to suffer the consequences!
如果你堅持要吃三份甜點，恐怕你會自作自受！
[ + obj + -ing verb ] I had to suffer her father moaning for half an hour on the phone last night!
昨晚我不得不忍受她父親在電話裡嘮叨抱怨了半個小時！
When you're working such long hours, it's inevitable that your marriage will start to suffer.
你老是這麼加班，婚姻難免會受影響。
Like a lot of his films, it suffers from being too long.
和他的其他很多電影一樣，這部電影也是有點太長了。

NONE: › with unwilling permission
經勉強同意，勉強允許地
› If someone does something under sufferance, they do it very unwillingly.
不情願地

example: He gave me a bed for a couple of nights but I felt I was there on sufferance.
他讓我住上幾個晚上，但我感覺自己在那裡並不受歡迎。
He only visits his parents under sufferance.
他探望父母時總是極不情願。

NONE: C2 a person who has or often gets a particular illness
病患

example: Almost 50 percent of cancer sufferers are treated successfully.
大約50%的癌症患者所接受的治療是奏效的。
A new drug may give new hope to thousands of hay-fever sufferers.
有種新藥可能會給數以千計的花粉熱患者帶來新希望。

NONE: B2 physical or mental pain that a person or animal is feeling
疼痛；折磨；痛苦

example: The war will cause widespread human suffering.
戰爭會給很多人帶來苦難。

NONE: › to be enough
足夠；滿足要求

example: I'm taking $400 - I think that should suffice.
我帶了400美元——我覺得應該夠了。

NONE: › it is enough to say
無需多說，只需說…就夠了

example: Suffice (it) to say, Mike won't be going to Tina's birthday party after what he said about her to her boss.
不用多說，麥克對蒂娜的老闆那樣說她之後，他是不會去參加她的生日聚會的。

NONE: › an amount of something that is enough, or the quality of being good enough
足量，充足

example: Will there still be a sufficiency of resources for our great-grandchildren?
還會有足夠的資源留給我們的子孫嗎？
There is concern over the sufficiency of plans to tackle the problem.
人們對計畫是否足以解決問題表示懷疑。

NONE: B2 enough for a particular purpose
足夠的，充足的
› to have eaten enough
吃飽了

example: This recipe should be sufficient for five people.
這份食譜應該足夠五個人吃。
It was thought that he'd committed the crime but there wasn't sufficient evidence to convict him.
人們都認為他是犯罪兇手，但沒有足夠證據將他定罪。
Opposite
insufficient
"Would you like some more stew?" "No thanks, I've had sufficient."
「你還想要一些燉肉嗎？」「不，謝謝！我已經吃飽了。」

NONE: B2 a letter or group of letters added at the end of a word to make a new word
後綴，詞尾

example: The suffix "-ness" added to the end of the word "sweet" forms the word "sweetness", changing an adjective into a noun.
後綴 -ness加在 sweet 之後構成 sweetness，把形容詞變成了名詞。

I or T: › to (cause someone to) die because of not having enough oxygen
› to prevent something or someone from improving or developing in a positive way

example: The report said that the victims had suffocated in the fumes.
報告說那些受害者是被煙熏死的。
She suffocated him by holding a pillow over his head.
她用枕頭壓在他的頭上，把他悶死。

NONE: › informal Something that is suffocating makes you feel uncomfortably hot or unable to breathe.
悶熱的；憋氣的
› preventing something or someone from improving or developing in a positive way
束縛的，阻止發展的；遏制的

example: I've got to open the window - it's suffocating in here!
我得把窗戶打開——這裡太悶了！
The book tells the story of a woman escaping from a suffocating marriage.
這本書講的是一個女人逃脫一段令人窒息的婚姻的故事。
It is a land of antiquated social rules and suffocating traditions.
這個地方依然保留著陳規陋習和令人倍感壓抑的傳統習俗。

NONE: › the right to vote in an election, especially to vote for representatives in a government
（尤指選舉議會等機構代表的）選舉權，投票權

example: universal suffrage (= the right of all adults to vote)
普選權

NONE: › a woman who campaigned for the right of women to vote, especially a member of the early 20th century British group of activitists led by Emmeline and Christabel Pankhurst
（20世紀初英國、澳大利亞和美國）為女性爭取選舉權團體的成員
› someone who supports suffrage, especially a supporter of the right of women to vote in the early 20th century
主張擴大選舉權者；（尤指20世紀初）支持女性選舉權者
› to spread through or over something completely
彌漫於；布滿；充滿

example: His voice was low and suffused with passion.
他的嗓音低沉，飽含熱情。

NONE: › a member of an Islamic religious group that tries to become united with God by living a simple life and by praying and meditating
蘇非派信徒（伊斯蘭教一個宗派的成員，主張生活儉樸、默禱沉思以達到人主合一）
